significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a measurable mismatch between "CoT-claimed and internally-attributed factors" predicts per-instance CoT unfaithfulness, a form-(iii) predictive coupling rather than merely the existence of an internal representation. It would establish both a phenomenon—reasoning omits a factor that influenced the answer—and a bounded mechanism—reliance on an injected cue despite a different verbal rationale—thereby fixing which outputs should be distrusted, although it would not establish a general mechanism for natural or deliberately deceptive reasoning; this targets the per-instance monitoring gap left by the aggregate perturbation measures in Lanham et al. (2023) and the biased-reasoning findings of Turpin et al. (2023). The negative branch would meaningfully rule out attribution-to-text mismatch as a dependable monitor even in controlled hidden-cue settings, but would not refute CoT monitoring generally; true and false outcomes are therefore distinguishable. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not earn this score: the specific claimed-factor/attributed-factor predictive coupling is what raises it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is a "per-instance faithfulness monitor" that can "flag mismatch between CoT-cited factors and attributed factors"; it is post hoc with respect to the unfaithful computation, but can be used ex ante with respect to trusting, gating, or acting on the resulting answer. After recalibration on another model, the claimed conclusion predicts a transferable relation—larger claimed-versus-attributed mismatch should indicate unfaithfulness—rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding an arbitrary direction. Its asserted scope spans task types and model scales but is principally grounded in hidden-cue cases, so likely downstream users include CoT-oversight researchers and practitioners auditing or gating model outputs, not users outside AI. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: broad safety interpretability alone supplies no monitor, while this claim names a usable auditing handle and predictive relation.
